issues.description: The problem statement's UML and text indicate getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int (see UML: +getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int), but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object (a custom type) and introduces a StudentCount class. This is a return-type mismatch that will confuse students about the expected return type and whether they should create/use a StudentCount class.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to specify that getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns a StudentCount (and document the StudentCount class), or (B) change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (the sum of inscribed and guest students) and remove/avoid using the StudentCount class. Prefer option B if the exercise intends to teach primitive returns; prefer option A if the StudentCount abstraction is intentional—then update the template and problem text to mention StudentCount so students know to use it.

issues.description: The problem statement / UML specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (primitive int return type), but the solution introduces a separate StudentCount class and implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object. This changes the expected type and names the 'total number of students' concept differently across artifacts, which can confuse students mapping the UML/requirements to the implementation and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type and naming across artifacts. Either change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return a primitive int (summing inscribed and guest students) to match the UML and problem text, or update the problem statement/UML to explicitly specify a StudentCount return type and mention the StudentCount class. Preferably return int to keep the API consistent with the UML and reduce student confusion.
